limits: Static trace only: no pinned bytes were executed and no live node, network, signer, or exchange state was used. The access census for each limit field covers direct accesses through the dispatcher object register inside the dispatcher FDE, cross-checked with two independent disassemblies; stores through a differently-based alias of the same object inside the dispatcher, and writes by callees other than the recorded record-helper behaviour, are not excluded. The last-writer analysis covers direct branches and the pinned jump-table slots; other jump-table targets were enumerated in the analysis and none lands in (final store, load] except the pinned ones. Who first set the object fields the final values are derived from (the bulk selector bytes, the twin sibling slots and source-object fields, and the incoming limit value on a downstream stage entry) sits above the traced window and is a stated boundary, as is the copy-a record helper effect on its record first qword and the writer of the twin-a stage result +0x28 field left open by #2501. Raw values are recorded mechanically; which Rust types or enum variants they belong to is not established. No Rust reconstruction is included or claimed.
